subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: latency & throughput follow-up / next A/B tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: latency & throughput follow-up / next A/B tests

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can run an apples-to-apples A/B: 

Summary of what we reviewed:
- Redwood internal microbench (representative 512-token request): p95 = ~120 ms, p99 = ~220 ms, sustained tokens/sec = ~3,200 (single model replica, batching=auto).
- Hyperscaler public endpoint (same model family, no KV cache): p95 = ~240 ms, p99 = ~420 ms, tokens/sec ~= ~1,800 under similar CPU/GPU profile.
- Key differentiators we highlighted: KV/prefix caching, continuous batching, lower kernel overhead for common sequence lengths, and optimized kernel selection for long-context variants.

What we need from you to proceed:
1) A small sample of your production traces (even 1-2k requests) so we can replay the distribution (attachment referenced if you prefer).
2) Your target SLOs (p95/p99 latency targets and acceptable tail). You mentioned p95 < 200 ms as a goal on the call — confirm.
3) Any constraints on test windows (time of day, traffic shaping), and whether we should include cache warmup windows.

Proposed A/B test plan (attached: latency_throughput_ab_test_plan.xlsx):
- Side-by-side runs against Redwood-hosted endpoint vs Hyperscaler endpoint using your sample traces.
- Run length: 24-48 hours, include warmup and steady-state windows.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens.
- Variants: with/without KV prefix cache; batching on vs conservative batching.

Attachments: redwood_globex_bench_summary_v2.pdf (summary of our initial bench), latency_throughput_ab_test_plan.xlsx

If you can drop the sample traces (or let us pull from a secure S3), Dylan (cc'd) and I will assemble the replay harness and calendar the run. Looking to get the A/B scheduled this week if possible.

Best,
Marissa

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: latency & throughput follow-up / next A/B tests

Marissa —

Appreciate the summary and plan. This aligns with what we discussed. A few quick answers and asks: 

1) We can share a trimmed set of traces — attached: globex_sample_traces.csv (approx 2,200 rows) that covers our 95th percentile request sizes and a mix of short/long prompts.
2) Confirming our business SLOs: p95 target = <200 ms, p99 target ideally <350 ms.
3) Yes to including cache warmup. For fairness, please include both cold-start and warmed variants.
4) Cost comparison is important for procurement — please include token-level cost estimates for the two runs (we need ballpark numbers to present to Finance).

Two asks for you: can Redwood run the side-by-side from the same region (us-west-2) so network variance is minimized? Also, can you expose per-request timing (so we can correlate slow tails with input length)?

We are good to move forward — Sara will coordinate windows on our side.

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah | Director of Platform Engineering | Globex Corporation
amit.shah@globex.com | +1 (206) 555-6821

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:12:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: latency & throughput follow-up / next A/B tests

Thanks Amit — copying the plan into actionable test steps below. I'll own the replay harness and measurements.

High-level test design (what we'll run):
- Two endpoints: Redwood-hosted (region: us-west-2) and Hyperscaler endpoint (region: us-west-2).
- Replay harness: k6 + custom replay to preserve inter-arrival time distribution. We'll tag each request with an id so we can join latency with input length.
- Run profile: 48 hours total, broken into: 2h cold start, 12h warmed steady-state pass 1, 12h warmed pass 2, 2h variable load spike windows (to measure queuing), remainder for artifacts collection.
- Metrics captured: per-request latency (start->first-token, full generation), p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue length, and cost counters.
- Variants: (A) caching enabled, batching auto (B) caching off, batching conservative (to simulate naive integration).
- Acceptance criteria: p95 < 200ms and p99 < 350ms for warmed steady-state; tokens/sec within 10% of Redwood baseline.

Technical notes:
- We'll replay your provided CSV; please indicate which column is the prompt length column and whether you want sampling by user-id to maintain session locality.
- We will produce a per-request CSV with timestamps that you can ingest.
- Cost calc: we'll output a cost-per-1M-tokens number for both endpoints; note that hyperscaler plans often include hidden egress/extra model switching costs — we'll surface assumptions.

Proposed schedule: start Friday 17 Jul 2026 02:00 UTC (evening PST) subject to your confirmation. We'll stream progress to the shared doc and send interim p95/p99 after 6 hours.

Attaching the concrete run script and measurement dashboard config: latency_throughput_ab_test_plan.xlsx (same as Marissa attached).

On quoting Amit: 
> We can share a trimmed set of traces — attached: globex_sample_traces.csv (approx 2,200 rows)

Amit — can you confirm the prompt-length column is named 'prompt_len' and whether you want us to preserve user session affinity?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
